name: CONUS / CONUS+
notes: The CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) states CONUS+ is 'continuing on this way the CONUS physics program started at the Brokdorf nuclear power plant' using 'the same four point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors produced for the former experiment, however refurbished'. This is the same collaboration and the same detector array, relocated to a new reactor site under a new name, so it is recorded as one experiment record (experiment:conus), not two lineage-linked records.
No INSPIRE experiment record was found for CONUS/CONUS+ (searched inspirehep.net/api/experiments; zero results), so external.inspire_experiment is left empty rather than guessed.
No official CONUS/CONUS+ website was found reachable (attempts at plausible MPIK URLs returned 404), so no website is recorded. This is a gap, not a considered absence.

The record name is 'CONUS / CONUS+' so that a search for 'CONUS+' finds this experiment; 'CONUS+' cannot be a separate alias because it matches the name once punctuation is ignored. The collaboration and detector records use the same 'X / X+' naming.

physics_goals.quote: The CONUS+ experiment aims to detect coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) of reactor antineutrinos on germanium nuclei in the fully coherent regime
physics_goals.value: Detect and precisely measure CEvNS of reactor antineutrinos on germanium nuclei in the fully coherent regime

summary.plain: A small, sensitive detector using ultra-pure germanium crystals to catch reactor antineutrinos gently bouncing off whole atomic nuclei, first run at a German nuclear plant and, after it closed, moved to a Swiss one under the name CONUS+.
summary.technical: Reactor CEvNS experiment using an array of four 1 kg point-contact HPGe spectrometers; ran as CONUS at the Brokdorf nuclear power plant, Germany (17.1 m baseline, 3.9 GWth core, 2018-2022), then relocated as CONUS+ to the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, Switzerland (20.7 m baseline, 3.6 GWth core, from November 2023), reporting a first direct 3.7σ observation of reactor CEvNS in January 2025.
